item.text: {"text":"Search found related 2024–2025 work, but no verified exact match for lightweight, jointly trained, randomly initialized title/description encoding inside BERT4Rec. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://dspace.hansung.ac.kr/bitstream/2024.oak/10390/2/AR_D2A1A2_ITS-Rec_%20A%20Sequential%20Recommendation%20Model%20Using%20Item%20Textual%20Information.pdf) combines item IDs with text, but uses pretrained BERT and reviews, outside the supplied constraints. [DenseRec (2025)](https://earl-workshop.github.io/pdf/recsys2025-workshops_paper_167.pdf) motivates retaining item-specific collaborative information: semantic similarity alone can miss differences in user appeal and context. Its pretrained content setup does not establish that scratch-trained text encoders improve this benchmark.\n\nA constraint-compatible experimental hypothesis is a small shared token embedding table with mean pooling or a shallow CNN over supplied titles/descriptions, projected and added through a learned gate to item ID embeddings. Train every component jointly through BERT4Rec masked-item loss; use the same fused item representation for candidate scoring within one network/checkpoint per category. This is an inferred design proposal, not a verified published result. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s Cloze objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690): masking an item must also remove its title/description from the input, otherwise content reveals the target. At inference, append the reserved mask token and score from its position. Shared text parameters could help sparse items, but improved fine-grained compatibility and macro validation HR@10 require measurement."}
